intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Trek through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and glacial moraines while enjoying breathtaking views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. The trail passes through traditional Gurung villages offering authentic cultural immersion alongside stunning Himalayan scenery.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of Nepal's most spectacular sunrises. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in a panoramic 180-degree view. The relatively short but rewarding hike takes about 1.5 hours from Ghorepani and is accessible to most fitness levels.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Homestay
experiences.description: Spend a night or two in a traditional Gurung village homestay, experiencing authentic Nepali mountain culture firsthand. Share home-cooked dal bhat, raksi (local millet wine), and momo dumplings with local families. Learn about Gurung traditions, shamanic rituals, and daily mountain life while sleeping in a traditional stone house with Himalayan views.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude and raw Himalayan beauty away from the crowds. Trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests to high-altitude meadows with close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). The 5-7 day route rewards trekkers with pristine nature, diverse wildlife, and a genuine off-the-beaten-path adventure.

experiences.name: Natural Hot Springs Soak at Jhinu Danda
experiences.description: Reward tired trekking muscles with a rejuvenating soak in the natural hot springs along the Modi Khola river at Jhinu Danda. The geothermal pools sit beside a rushing glacial river surrounded by lush jungle, creating a magical contrast of hot and cold. A perfect rest-day activity mid-trek, the springs are easily accessible via a short 20-minute downhill walk from Chhomrong village.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange a pre-booked budget taxi or airport bus to your accommodation. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the trek ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or skip
meals.lunch: Meal on flight or airport snack
meals.dinner: Quick late-night dal bhat or noodle soup at a nearby local teahouse near the resort (~NPR 300–500)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Nepali Rupees (NPR) ready for taxi and tips. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM. Stay hydrated after the flight. Confirm trek permits and gear checklist before sleeping.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and enjoy a light breakfast at the resort. Head to Pokhara (if not already there) via tourist bus from Kathmandu — a scenic 6–7 hour ride (~NPR 700–1000). Alternatively, take a short flight (~NPR 6000–8000 one way) for faster access. Enjoy views of the Annapurna range en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara. Visit the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) office to obtain your TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP permit) — essential for the trek (~NPR 3000 total for both). Explore Lakeside Pokhara market for any last-minute budget trekking gear.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Phewa Lake waterfront at Lakeside. Enjoy the sunset reflecting off the lake with Annapurna South in the background. Explore the vibrant Lakeside bazaar for souvenirs and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Included at resort or local tea shop — eggs, toast, tea (~NPR 200–300)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a roadside dhaba during bus journey (~NPR 250–400)
meals.dinner: Thakali set meal at a local Pokhara restaurant near Lakeside (~NPR 400–600)

day_by_day.notes: Obtain TIMS Card and ACAP Permit before starting the trek — these are mandatory. Budget trekkers can buy or rent trekking poles, sleeping bag liners, and rain gear in Pokhara at affordable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning jeep or local bus from Pokhara to Nayapul (~NPR 300–500, 1.5 hours). Begin the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trek from Nayapul. Trek through Birethanti (1025m) — a charming riverside village where permit checks are done. Continue trekking uphill through lush rhododendron and oak forests toward Hile.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Hile to Tikhedhunga (1480m) — approximately 2–3 hours of moderate hiking. Enjoy stunning views of terraced farmlands and waterfalls. Rest at a teahouse and refill water bottles (use purification tablets to save money).
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a budget teahouse in Tikhedhunga. Rest tired legs, socialize with fellow trekkers, and enjoy the peaceful mountain ambiance. Review the next day's route on your trail map.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs with tea at Pokhara before departure (~NPR 200–300)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a Birethanti teahouse (~NPR 350–500)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Tikhedhunga teahouse (~NPR 400–600, includes unlimited refills)

day_by_day.notes: Dal bhat is the best budget meal on the trek — many teahouses offer unlimited refills. Carry a reusable water bottle and purification tablets to avoid buying plastic bottles. Trek distance today: approximately 10 km.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Tikhedhunga. Climb the famous stone staircase — over 3,000 steps — ascending steeply through forests to Ulleri (2073m). This is one of the most challenging sections of the lower trek. Take breaks and enjoy panoramic views of the Modi Khola valley below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Ulleri through rhododendron forests to Banthanti (2250m) and on to Ghorepani (2860m). Arrive by early afternoon. Ghorepani is a popular trekker hub with stunning views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South on clear days.
day_by_day.evening: Acclimatize gently at Ghorepani. Visit the small local market for snacks. Enjoy a warm cup of ginger lemon honey tea at your teahouse while watching the alpenglow on the Annapurna range at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and banana at Tikhedhunga teahouse (~NPR 250–350)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice or tsampa porridge at Ulleri (~NPR 350–500)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with pickles and papad at Ghorepani teahouse (~NPR 450–650)

day_by_day.notes: The Tikhedhunga to Ulleri climb is steep — start early to avoid midday heat. Ghorepani gets cold at night (October temperatures can drop to 2–5°C) so layer up. Trek distance today: approximately 11 km, elevation gain ~1400m.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn hike (depart 4:30–5:00 AM) to Poon Hill (3210m) — one of the most iconic sunrise viewpoints in Nepal. Watch the sunrise illuminate Dhaulagiri (8167m), Annapurna I (8091m), Machapuchare (6993m), and over a dozen Himalayan peaks. A truly breathtaking budget highlight of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for a late breakfast, then continue trekking toward Tadapani (2630m) through dense rhododendron forests. The trail winds through beautiful mixed forest with occasional monkey sightings. Arrive at Tadapani by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Tadapani teahouse with views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Write in your travel journal, share stories with other trekkers, and enjoy the serene mountain atmosphere. The night sky here is spectacular — look for the Milky Way on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Hot lemon tea before Poon Hill hike, then full breakfast after return — eggs, toast, porridge (~NPR 300–450)
meals.lunch: Packed snack or light meal at a trail teahouse (~NPR 300–400)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Tadapani teahouse (~NPR 400–600)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headlamp and warm jacket for the Poon Hill pre-dawn hike — it is cold and dark. Entry fee for Poon Hill viewpoint: NPR 100. Trek distance today: approximately 12 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2170m) — a long but rewarding descent through forested ridges with stunning views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). The trail passes through Gurung villages with traditional stone houses and mani walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong — the last major village before the Annapurna Sanctuary. Explore the village, visit the small monastery, and enjoy sweeping views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli towering above. Stock up on snacks and chocolates here as prices increase higher up the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a budget teahouse in Chhomrong. Enjoy the warm hospitality of Gurung families who run many of the teahouses. Rest well — the trail ahead gets more challenging.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and tea at Tadapani (~NPR 250–350)
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and bread at a trail teahouse (~NPR 300–450)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with seasonal vegetables at Chhomrong teahouse (~NPR 450–650)

day_by_day.notes: Buy extra snacks (energy bars, biscuits, nuts) in Chhomrong — they become significantly more expensive at higher altitudes. Chhomrong has the last reliable ATM-accessible area before the sanctuary. Trek distance today: approximately 10 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong descending stone steps to Sinuwa (2360m), then continue through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2310m). The trail follows the Modi Khola river gorge with dramatic canyon walls rising on both sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Bamboo to Dovan (2600m) through increasingly dense forest. The trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary — a glacial amphitheater surrounded by some of the world's highest peaks. Watch for signs of wildlife including Himalayan tahr and langur monkeys.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Himalaya Hotel (2920m) — a cluster of teahouses at the edge of the sanctuary. Temperatures drop noticeably here. Enjoy the dramatic gorge views, cozy up by the teahouse fire, and prepare mentally for the high-altitude terrain ahead.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal porridge with nuts and tea at Chhomrong (~NPR 250–350)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at Bamboo teahouse (~NPR 400–550)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or fried noodles at Himalaya Hotel (~NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Prices increase significantly inside the sanctuary — expect to pay 30–50% more for food and accommodation. The trail through the gorge can be slippery — trek poles are highly recommended. Trek distance today: approximately 11 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel to Deurali (3230m) through the narrow Modi Khola gorge. This section can be affected by avalanche risk in winter but is generally safe in October. The canyon walls narrow dramatically — an awe-inspiring natural spectacle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Deurali to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3700m. Arrive at MBC — a high plateau with jaw-dropping 360-degree views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Annapurna South, and Hiunchuli. The sacred Machhapuchhre peak is off-limits to climbers.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and acclimatize at MBC. Watch the sunset paint the surrounding peaks in shades of gold, orange, and pink. The stars at this altitude are extraordinary — enjoy some of the clearest night skies of your life. Keep warm with layers as temperatures drop below freezing.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast with ginger tea at Himalaya Hotel (~NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and bread at Deurali — garlic helps with altitude (~NPR 450–600)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse (~NPR 550–750)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness can begin at 3000m+ — watch for headache, nausea, and dizziness. Drink plenty of water (3–4 liters/day). Garlic soup is a local remedy for altitude sickness. Do not ascend if you feel unwell. Trek distance today: approximately 9 km.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start (4:00–4:30 AM) from MBC to reach Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4130m for sunrise. The final 2-hour climb crosses a glacial moraine with stunning views unfolding at every step. Arrive at ABC to witness one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas — surrounded by Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend time at ABC exploring the glacier area, taking photographs, and soaking in the once-in-a-lifetime panorama. Sign the teahouse guest book. Begin the descent back to MBC and continue down to Dovan (2600m) — descending is faster but hard on the knees.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Dovan teahouse. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers over a warm meal. Rest your legs — today involves significant elevation change. Reflect on the incredible achievement of reaching 4130m.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea or instant noodles before ABC hike, then full breakfast on return to MBC (~NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Snack bars and trail mix carried from MBC (save money at altitude)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with extra portions at Dovan teahouse (~NPR 550–750)

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trek! Dress in all your warmest layers for the pre-dawn ABC hike — temperatures at 4130m in October can be -10°C or colder. The descent from ABC to Dovan in one day is long (approximately 16 km) but saves on accommodation costs.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan back through Bamboo and Sinuwa, retracing the trail through the bamboo forest and rhododendron groves. The descent feels much faster and your legs are now well-conditioned. Enjoy the familiar forest scenery from a fresh perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descent to Chhomrong (2170m). Stop at the small Chhomrong monastery for a moment of reflection. Visit a local Gurung family's home for tea if invited — a genuine cultural experience at no or minimal cost.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Chhomrong teahouse — a welcome return to lower altitude where breathing feels easier. Enjoy a celebratory hot shower (budget ~NPR 200–300 extra) to wash off the trail dust. Share trek stories with other returning hikers.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and boiled eggs at Dovan teahouse (~NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice at Sinuwa teahouse (~NPR 400–550)
meals.dinner: Thakali dal bhat with raksi (local millet wine) at Chhomrong — a small celebration (~NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 13 km. Knees can ache on long descents — trekking poles help significantly. You have now completed the most challenging section of the trek. Well done!

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong to Jhinu Danda (1780m) — a short but steep descent. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs along the Modi Khola river. Arrive by late morning and spend time soaking in the therapeutic hot springs (~NPR 200 entry) — the perfect reward for tired trekking muscles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Jhinu Danda to New Bridge and then climb to Landruk (1565m) — a traditional Gurung village with beautiful terraced fields and mountain views. Explore the village lanes and interact with local families.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a budget guesthouse in Landruk. Enjoy the warmth of lower altitude. Watch the sunset over the Modi Khola valley and the distant Annapurna range — a peaceful end to a rewarding day.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancakes and tea at Chhomrong (~NPR 250–350)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~NPR 400–550)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice at Landruk guesthouse (~NPR 400–600)

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are a must-do — budget trekkers should not skip this. Bring a towel and flip flops. Trek distance today: approximately 10 km. This is a relatively relaxed day compared to recent days.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Landruk through terraced hillsides and Gurung villages to Tolka (1700m) and then down to Pothana (1890m). The trail offers some of the best unobstructed views of Machapuchare and the Annapurna massif on clear October mornings — perfect for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Pothana through forests to Dhampus (1650m) — one of the most picturesque villages in the Annapurna foothills with stunning panoramic mountain views. Explore the village, visit local homes, and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere. Consider a short optional hike to a nearby viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight in Dhampus. Enjoy a quiet village evening with local families. The community here is very welcoming to budget trekkers. Watch for the Annapurna range glowing in the last light of the day.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with hot milk and tea at Landruk (~NPR 250–350)
meals.lunch: Egg fried rice at Tolka teahouse (~NPR 350–500)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with local spinach at Dhampus guesthouse (~NPR 400–550)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — book teahouses in advance or arrive early in the afternoon to secure budget rooms. Trek distance today: approximately 11 km. You are now on the final stretch back toward Pokhara.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning trek from Dhampus down to Phedi (1130m) — approximately 2 hours of pleasant downhill walking through terraced farmland and forest. Catch a local minibus or jeep from Phedi back to Pokhara (~NPR 200–300, 45 minutes). Arrive in Pokhara by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Celebrate completing the Annapurna Base Camp trek! Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (~NPR 400 entry) — a world-class museum dedicated to Himalayan exploration and the mountains of Nepal. Explore the exhibits on Annapurna and the history of mountaineering.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride on Phewa Lake (~NPR 500–700 for a rowing boat rental) — paddle toward the Barahi Temple island and enjoy reflections of the Annapurna range on the calm lake. Return to Lakeside for a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Last trail breakfast — porridge and eggs at Dhampus (~NPR 250–350)
meals.lunch: Momos (Nepali dumplings) and chai at a Pokhara street stall (~NPR 150–250)
meals.dinner: Celebratory Newari set meal or wood-fired pizza at a Lakeside restaurant (~NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: You have completed approximately 110+ km of trekking over 11 days — an incredible achievement! Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner tonight within budget. Get laundry done in Pokhara (~NPR 100–150/kg) before heading back to Kathmandu.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) above Pokhara — hike up or take a boat across Phewa Lake and then climb for 30 minutes (~NPR 200 boat). Enjoy the last panoramic views of the entire Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. A peaceful and reflective final morning in Nepal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara Lakeside for last-minute souvenir shopping — Tibetan handicrafts, Thangka paintings, prayer flags, and woolen goods are excellent budget souvenirs. Head to the bus park and take a tourist bus or local bus back to Kathmandu (~NPR 700–1000, 6–7 hours) or a short flight (~NPR 6000–8000).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kathmandu. Spend the evening in Thamel — Kathmandu's backpacker hub. Explore the vibrant night market, browse bookshops, and enjoy a final Nepali meal. Pack, organize trekking permits and photos as souvenirs, and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with jam and butter tea near the Stupa (~NPR 200–300)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a local Pokhara restaurant before departure (~NPR 350–500)
meals.dinner: Nepali thali with kheer (rice pudding) dessert at a Thamel restaurant (~NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your TIMS card and ACAP permit as memorable souvenirs of your trek. Budget summary: Total estimated trek cost excluding flights — approximately NPR 25,000–35,000 (USD 185–260) for 14 days including accommodation, meals, and permits. Nepal is one of the world's best value trekking destinations!

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer to your accommodation. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, Annapurna region. Freshen up and rest.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival if available

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. Keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Confirm your trekking permits (TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) are arranged in advance or plan to obtain them in Pokhara the next day. Hydrate well and sleep early to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, head to Pokhara city to obtain necessary trekking permits — TIMS Card and ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) from the Nepal Tourism Board office. Budget around NPR 3,000–4,000 total for permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Pokhara's Lakeside (Phewa Lake area). Stroll along the lake promenade, browse local trekking gear shops to pick up any missing essentials, and enjoy the stunning views of the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) peaks from the lakeside.
day_by_day.evening: Relax by Phewa Lake at sunset — one of Nepal's most iconic views. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range lakeside restaurant and do a final gear check for the upcoming trek.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Momos (dumplings) and thukpa (noodle soup) at a local Pokhara eatery near the permit office — approximately NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat (lentil soup, rice, vegetables, and pickles) at a lakeside mid-range restaurant such as Moondance Restaurant or similar — approximately NPR 700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Carry passport-size photos and passport copies for permit applications. Confirm your trekking route with your guide or resort staff. Stock up on snacks, water purification tablets, and any last-minute trekking supplies in Pokhara's Lakeside market.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the resort. Drive or take a local taxi/jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (approximately 1.5 hours, NPR 1,500–2,000 by private jeep). Begin the classic Annapurna Circuit / Poon Hill trek starting point. Trek from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 3–4 hours, 7 km). The trail winds through terraced fields, Modi Khola river crossings, and small Gurung villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tikhedhunga (1,540m). Explore the charming village, interact with local Gurung and Magar communities, and rest at your teahouse. The trail passes through lush subtropical forests and offers early Himalayan views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a mid-range teahouse in Tikhedhunga. Enjoy a warm meal and socialize with fellow trekkers. Early bedtime to prepare for the challenging climb the next day.

meals.breakfast: Eggs, toast, and tea at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or dal bhat at a small teahouse along the trail — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at the Tikhedhunga teahouse — NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season in Nepal — trails and teahouses can be busy. Book teahouses in advance if possible. Pace yourself on Day 1 of trekking. Altitude at Tikhedhunga is manageable but start practicing slow, steady hiking habits.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 6:00 AM for an early start. Trek from Tikhedhunga to Ghorepani (2,860m) — approximately 5–6 hours covering 10 km. The trail climbs steeply through a famous stone staircase with over 3,000 steps through dense rhododendron and oak forests. This is one of the more demanding sections of the trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghorepani by early afternoon. Rest and acclimatize. Explore the village and enjoy panoramic views of Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna South, and Hiunchuli from the village itself.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from the village surroundings. Warm up with ginger tea or hot chocolate at your teahouse. Prepare for the 4:00 AM wake-up call for Poon Hill sunrise the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or pancakes with honey at Tikhedhunga teahouse — NPR 300–500
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a trail teahouse in Ulleri — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with seasonal vegetables at Ghorepani teahouse — NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: The climb to Ghorepani is steep and tiring — take regular breaks and stay hydrated. Altitude increase is significant today; watch for early signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea). Ghorepani has reliable teahouses with decent facilities. Charge electronics here as power may be limited higher up.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:00 AM. Hike 45 minutes by headlamp to Poon Hill (3,210m) to witness one of Nepal's most celebrated sunrises over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. The panoramic view includes Annapurna I, II, III, IV, South, Machhapuchhre, Dhaulagiri, and more. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,630m) — approximately 4–5 hours through magnificent rhododendron forests. In October, the forest is lush and the views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre are spectacular throughout the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tadapani. Rest and enjoy the mountain panorama. The village sits in a clearing with sweeping Himalayan views. Enjoy a quiet evening at the teahouse.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea at Poon Hill viewpoint (vendors present), then full breakfast back at teahouse — eggs, toast, and porridge — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Snack bar or packed lunch on the Tadapani trail — NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice or pasta at Tadapani teahouse — NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee is NPR 100. Dress warmly for the pre-dawn hike — temperatures can drop to near freezing at this altitude in October. Bring a headlamp with fresh batteries. The Ghorepani–Tadapani trail is moderately challenging with some steep descents.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m) — approximately 4–5 hours. The trail descends steeply through forests and terraced hillsides before reaching the large Gurung village of Chhomrong, the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy close-up views of Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chhomrong village — one of the largest and most developed villages on the Annapurna Sanctuary trek. Visit the local monastery, interact with Gurung locals, and enjoy the stunning terrace views of the surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at your teahouse in Chhomrong. This is a good place to rest before entering the more remote Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy a hearty dinner and plan the next day's route.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with hot milk and tea at Tadapani teahouse — NPR 300–500
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a trail teahouse — NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Chicken or vegetable curry with rice at Chhomrong teahouse — NPR 700–900

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong has better facilities including hot showers (extra charge ~NPR 200–300) and reliable charging points. Stock up on snacks and water purification supplies as prices increase significantly higher up the sanctuary trail. This is the last major village with good connectivity.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong to Dovan (2,600m) via Sinuwa and Bamboo — approximately 5–6 hours. The trail descends dramatically into the Modi Khola gorge, crosses the river, and re-ascends through dense bamboo forests and rhododendron groves. The canyon walls rise dramatically on both sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Dovan. Rest and take in the dramatic gorge scenery. The trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary proper here — the landscape becomes wilder and more remote. Enjoy the sounds of the river and forest.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your teahouse at Dovan. The village is small with a few basic teahouses. Enjoy a warm meal and rest well — the altitude increase becomes more significant from here.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and tea at Chhomrong teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Bamboo teahouse — NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Dovan teahouse — NPR 700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Prices at teahouses increase significantly once inside the sanctuary — budget NPR 1,000–1,500 per meal on average. The trail from Chhomrong involves a steep descent and re-ascent — take your time. Watch for leeches on the lower trail sections (less common in October than monsoon season but possible). Carry sufficient water.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3,700m) via Himalaya Hotel and Deurali — approximately 5–6 hours. The trail climbs steadily through the narrowing gorge with increasingly dramatic mountain scenery. Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak, 6,993m) dominates the view ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC). The views here are absolutely stunning — surrounded by towering Himalayan peaks. Rest and acclimatize. Short exploratory walk around the base camp area. Take in the sacred Machhapuchhre peak (closed to climbing as it is considered sacred).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the sunset alpenglow on the surrounding peaks from MBC. The sky at this altitude is incredibly clear in October — excellent for stargazing after dark. Rest early for the push to Annapurna Base Camp the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Dovan teahouse — NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Hot soup and bread at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — NPR 700–1,000
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse — NPR 1,000–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness risk increases significantly from here. Watch for symptoms: persistent headache, dizziness, loss of appetite, nausea. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water daily. Sleep at MBC (3,700m) rather than pushing to ABC (4,130m) on the same day to allow proper acclimatization.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (5:00–5:30 AM) and trek from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) — approximately 2 hours. Arrive at ABC for sunrise — one of the most breathtaking experiences in all of Himalayan trekking. You are surrounded by a 360-degree amphitheater of peaks: Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Machhapuchhre, Hiunchuli, and more.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon exploring Annapurna Base Camp. Walk around the glacier moraine area, photograph the stunning peaks, and soak in the achievement of reaching 4,130m. Begin descent back to MBC or Deurali after lunch to avoid spending too many nights at high altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight at Deurali or Himalaya Hotel teahouse on the descent. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers over a warm meal.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits at ABC — NPR 500–800
meals.lunch: Instant noodles or soup at ABC teahouse — NPR 800–1,200
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Deurali or Himalaya Hotel teahouse — NPR 900–1,200

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trek. October offers excellent clear skies with minimal cloud cover — maximize time at ABC in the morning before afternoon clouds typically build. Do not rush the descent — take it steady. Altitude descent will naturally improve how you feel. Stay hydrated throughout.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Deurali/Himalaya Hotel back to Chhomrong — approximately 6–7 hours. The descent retraces the ascent route through Dovan, Bamboo, and Sinuwa. The dramatic gorge scenery looks entirely different on the way down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Chhomrong by early afternoon. Enjoy a well-deserved hot shower (NPR 200–300) and rest your legs. Chhomrong feels luxurious after the high-altitude teahouses — hot meals, better facilities, and reliable electricity.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of the Annapurna Sanctuary section of the trek. Enjoy a celebratory dinner at Chhomrong. Chat with other trekkers and share stories from ABC.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at Deurali teahouse — NPR 600–800
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at Bamboo teahouse — NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta (teahouse style) with apple pie at Chhomrong — NPR 800–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Descents are tough on the knees — use trekking poles if available and take the stone steps carefully. Your body will feel the accumulated fatigue of the trek by now — rest well at Chhomrong. If you feel unwell or overly fatigued, consider an extra rest day here.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back toward Ghandruk (1,940m) — approximately 4–5 hours through terraced hillsides and rhododendron forests. Ghandruk is one of the largest and most beautiful Gurung villages in Nepal, with traditional stone houses and cobblestone paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ghandruk village thoroughly — visit the Ghandruk Gurung Museum (small entry fee) to learn about Gurung culture, traditions, and the history of Gurkha soldiers. Walk through the stone-paved lanes and interact with local villagers.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre from Ghandruk's terraces — some of the most photogenic mountain views in Nepal. Relax at your teahouse and enjoy a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Chhomrong teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a trail teahouse — NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Traditional Gurung meal (gundruk soup, dhido, and vegetables) at Ghandruk teahouse — NPR 700–900

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk is a culturally rich village and a highlight beyond just the trekking. The Gurung Museum is small but informative and worth the visit. Ghandruk has better teahouse options — book ahead during peak October season. This is a gentler day after the demanding Sanctuary section.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Ghandruk to Landruk (1,565m) and then down to Phedi — approximately 3–4 hours of pleasant downhill trekking through terraced fields and forests. Alternatively, take the trail via Australian Camp for panoramic Annapurna views before descending.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Phedi, arrange a local taxi or jeep back to Pokhara (approximately 1 hour, NPR 1,000–1,500). Check back into your accommodation in the Pokhara/Annapurna area. Enjoy a long hot shower, rest, and recovery. Visit a local massage parlor in Pokhara for a traditional Nepali or Ayurvedic massage (NPR 1,500–2,500 for 60–90 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of your trek with a proper sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Pokhara's Lakeside area. Enjoy a cold drink and reflect on the incredible journey.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Ghandruk teahouse — eggs, toast, porridge — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a trail teahouse or in Phedi — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Grilled fish (Pokhara is famous for fresh lake fish), or continental meal at a Lakeside restaurant — NPR 1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: The trek is essentially complete. Take your time on the final descent and savor the last trail views. Pokhara will feel wonderfully comfortable after 10 days of teahouse living. Treat yourself to a good meal and a massage — your legs have earned it.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry NPR 400) — an excellent museum dedicated to the history of Himalayan mountaineering, the mountain ranges, and local cultures. Highly recommended for trekking enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat ride on Phewa Lake to Tal Barahi Temple — a small Hindu temple on an island in the lake (boat NPR 400–600 round trip, small temple donation). Alternatively, hike up to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of the Annapurna range and Pokhara city — approximately 1.5 hours round trip hike or short taxi ride.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pokhara's Lakeside market for souvenirs — Nepali handicrafts, thangka paintings, pashmina shawls, and trekking memorabilia. Enjoy a final lakeside dinner in Pokhara.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast with fresh juice at a Lakeside café — NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Newari cuisine (beaten rice, black lentils, spiced meat) at a local Newari restaurant — NPR 600–800
meals.dinner: Set dinner menu at a mid-range Lakeside restaurant — NPR 1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: This is a well-deserved rest day — do not over-schedule. Allow your body to recover from 10 days of trekking. The International Mountain Museum is genuinely fascinating for anyone who has just completed an Annapurna trek. Shop for quality souvenirs — bargaining is expected and accepted in Pokhara markets.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara/Annapurna region. Enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the resort. If time permits, take an early morning walk along the Phewa Lake promenade for final views of the Annapurna range reflected in the lake — one of Nepal's most iconic images. Pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Pokhara Regional Airport for a domestic flight to Kathmandu (approximately 25 minutes, NPR 5,000–8,000 one way) or arrange a tourist bus/private vehicle (approximately 7–8 hours, NPR 1,500–3,000). Depending on your onward international flight schedule, either explore Kathmandu's Thamel area or head directly to Tribhuvan International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Nepal with incredible memories of the Annapurna region. If staying overnight in Kathmandu, enjoy a final Nepali dinner in Thamel — try a rooftop restaurant for a fitting farewell.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort — enjoy every last bite — NPR 500–800
meals.lunch: Quick meal at Pokhara airport or en route to Kathmandu — NPR 400–700
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Thamel, Kathmandu — traditional Nepali thali or international cuisine — NPR 1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your domestic flight booking in advance — Pokhara to Kathmandu flights can fill up during peak October season. Allow at least 3–4 hours before your international departure for check-in, security, and immigration at Tribhuvan International Airport. Carry trekking permits and any receipts as souvenirs — they make wonderful mementos. Declare any items purchased over customs allowance limits.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of Nepal's most spectacular sunrises. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in a panoramic 180-degree view. The relatively short but rewarding hike takes about 1.5 hours from Ghorepani and is accessible to most fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Rest — Flight UA lands at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Tribhuvan International Airport to your luxury accommodation in the Annapurna region via private chauffeured vehicle arranged by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival & Rest — No afternoon activities scheduled. Settle into your Beachfront suite at Aegean Bliss Resort, enjoy a welcome drink and light refreshments prepared by the resort's hospitality team.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival welcome: Private check-in experience with resort concierge, complimentary welcome amenity basket featuring local Nepali teas, dried fruits, and artisan chocolates. Unwind with a warm bath and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or pre-arrival
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or pre-arrival
meals.dinner: Late-night private in-room dining: Light Nepali dal bhat set with organic lentils, seasonal vegetables, and handmade roti, paired with warm masala chai — available until 01:00 via 24-hour room service

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — rest is the priority. Keep luggage accessible for an early unpack. Set alarms for Day 2 acclimatization activities. Hydrate well as altitude adjustment begins immediately upon arrival in the Annapurna region.

day_by_day.morning: Acclimatization Morning Walk & Resort Orientation — Begin with a gentle 1–2 hour guided walk through the resort grounds and surrounding village pathways. Your private guide will introduce you to the local flora, Gurung village architecture, and the first breathtaking views of the Annapurna massif. Pace is intentionally slow to assist altitude adjustment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pokhara Lakeside Exploration — Transfer by private vehicle to Pokhara's Phewa Lake area. Enjoy a private luxury boat ride on Phewa Lake with views of the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) peaks reflected in the water. Visit the Tal Barahi Temple on the lake's island. Browse high-end artisan shops for Pashmina shawls and Thangka paintings.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Viewing from Sarangkot Viewpoint — Private vehicle transfer to Sarangkot for golden-hour panoramic views of the entire Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Return to resort for a curated welcome dinner with the resort's executive chef.

meals.breakfast: Lavish resort breakfast buffet featuring freshly baked Nepali breads, organic eggs cooked to order, local honey, seasonal fruit platters, and a selection of Himalayan herbal teas and artisan coffees
meals.lunch: Lakeside fine dining at Caffe Concerto or Moondance Restaurant, Pokhara — enjoy wood-fired pizza, fresh salads, and Nepali fusion cuisine with panoramic lake views
meals.dinner: Private chef's table dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated 4-course Nepali-continental fusion menu featuring yak cheese appetizers, pumpkin soup, grilled river trout, and cardamom panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Drink at least 3–4 liters of water today. Avoid alcohol on Day 2 to assist acclimatization. Carry light layers as temperatures can drop significantly after sunset at Sarangkot.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Yoga & Meditation Session — Begin at 06:00 with a private sunrise yoga and pranayama session on the resort's mountain-view terrace led by a certified Himalayan yoga instructor. The session focuses on breathwork to support high-altitude adaptation. Follow with a guided 30-minute meditation overlooking the Annapurna range.
day_by_day.afternoon: World Peace Pagoda Hike — Embark on a moderately scenic hike to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) above Pokhara. Your private guide leads you through forested trails with rhododendron and oak trees. At the summit, enjoy 360-degree views of Pokhara Valley, Phewa Lake, and the Himalayas. Approximately 3–4 hours round trip at a comfortable pace.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Nepali Cultural Evening — Return to resort for a private Gurung cultural performance arranged exclusively for your group, featuring traditional Ghatu dance, live sarangi music, and folk storytelling by local community artists. Enjoy curated cocktails and canapés during the performance.

meals.breakfast: Healthy power breakfast: Acai bowls, Himalayan granola with yak milk yogurt, smoked salmon on multigrain toast, fresh-pressed juices, and bulletproof coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the trail near World Peace Pagoda — resort-prepared luxury picnic basket with gourmet sandwiches, fruit, energy bars, local cheese, and thermos of Nepali butter tea
meals.dinner: Thakali cuisine dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — Mustang lamb curry, buckwheat roti, gundruk (fermented greens), and sel roti dessert with local raksi (optional)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes for the World Peace Pagoda trail. Apply sunscreen and carry a light rain jacket as October afternoons can bring brief showers. The cultural evening begins at 19:30.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic Mountain Flight or Helicopter Sunrise Tour — Depart at 06:30 for an exclusive private helicopter sunrise tour over the Annapurna Sanctuary and Machhapuchhre Base Camp area. Witness the first golden light illuminating Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, and the iconic Fishtail peak from the air. Land briefly at a high-altitude viewpoint for photographs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ghandruk Village Trek — Drive to Nayapul and begin a guided trek to the traditional Gurung village of Ghandruk (1,940m). Walk through terraced fields, rhododendron forests, and stone-paved trails. Visit the Gurung Museum and interact with local weavers producing handmade Pashmina and Dhaka textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Lodge Dinner in Ghandruk — Overnight at a premium teahouse or luxury mountain lodge in Ghandruk. Enjoy the crisp mountain air and a private dinner prepared by the lodge chef with locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-departure breakfast at resort: Croissants, boiled eggs, fruit, and strong Nepali coffee served at 05:45
meals.lunch: Authentic Gurung home-cooked meal in Ghandruk — dal bhat, nettle soup, potato curry, and fermented pickle served in a traditional stone house
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner: Garlic soup, Annapurna trout, roasted vegetables, Nepali cheese board, and warm apple cider

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tour subject to weather conditions — resort will confirm the evening before. Bring your camera with extra batteries as photo opportunities are extraordinary. Pack an overnight bag for the Ghandruk stay; main luggage remains at the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Ghandruk to Tadapani Trek — Rise at dawn for sunrise views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from Ghandruk. After breakfast, begin the scenic trek to Tadapani (2,630m) through dense rhododendron and magnolia forest. The trail offers continuous Himalayan panoramas and excellent birdwatching opportunities including Himalayan Monal pheasants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tadapani Exploration & Nature Walk — Arrive in Tadapani by early afternoon. Explore the surrounding ridgeline with your guide, identifying alpine flora and local wildlife. Enjoy a private photography session with a professional mountain photographer arranged by the resort to capture the dramatic Annapurna skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Stargazing & Mountain Reflection — At altitude with minimal light pollution, enjoy a guided stargazing session with a portable telescope provided by your guide. The October skies over the Annapurna region offer extraordinary visibility of the Milky Way, constellations, and planets.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast in Ghandruk: Tibetan bread with honey and butter, porridge with dried fruits, boiled eggs, and masala tea
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at a scenic rest point — resort-packed gourmet bento box with sandwiches, energy bars, local apples, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Luxury teahouse dinner in Tadapani: Vegetable thukpa (noodle soup), sautéed mountain mushrooms, steamed momos with chili sauce, and hot chocolate

day_by_day.notes: The Ghandruk–Tadapani trail is approximately 4–5 hours at a comfortable trekking pace. Altitude increases to 2,630m — monitor for any headaches or dizziness. Dress in warm layers as evening temperatures drop to 5–8°C in October.

day_by_day.morning: Tadapani to Ghorepani Trek — Depart after sunrise for the iconic trail toward Ghorepani (2,860m), passing through ancient rhododendron forests that blaze with color even in October. The trail crosses ridges offering alternating views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. This is one of the most photographically rewarding sections of the entire circuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ghorepani Arrival & Village Exploration — Arrive in Ghorepani by early afternoon. Check into a premium mountain lodge. Explore the village, visit the local monastery, and interact with Magar and Gurung community members. Your guide provides cultural context and translates conversations with local residents.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-Poon Hill Preparation & Briefing — Your private guide conducts a detailed briefing for tomorrow's pre-dawn Poon Hill sunrise hike. Review gear, headlamps, warm clothing layers, and the 04:00 wake-up call plan. Early dinner and rest by 20:30.

meals.breakfast: Tadapani lodge breakfast: Pancakes with local honey, scrambled eggs, sausage, seasonal fruit, and ginger lemon tea
meals.lunch: Mid-trail lunch at a Magar village rest stop: Fresh vegetable soup, rice and lentil dish, and sweet lassi
meals.dinner: Early premium lodge dinner in Ghorepani: Pumpkin soup, yak steak with roasted potatoes, mixed greens, and warm brownie with cream — served at 18:30 to allow for early rest

day_by_day.notes: Early bedtime is strongly recommended tonight — wake-up for Poon Hill is at 04:00. Confirm headlamp batteries, warm jacket, gloves, and hat are ready. The lodge will prepare a thermos of hot tea for the early morning hike.

day_by_day.morning: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike — Wake at 04:00 for the signature experience of the entire journey. Depart by 04:30 with headlamps for the 45-minute ascent to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m). Witness one of Nepal's most spectacular sunrises as golden light progressively illuminates Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre in a breathtaking sequential display. Your private photographer captures the moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descent to Tikhedhunga & Drive to Pokhara — After savoring the summit experience, descend back to Ghorepani for a hearty breakfast, then continue descending via Ulleri to Tikhedhunga or Nayapul for private vehicle pickup. Scenic drive back to Pokhara and return to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Spa Recovery Evening — Upon return to the resort, indulge in a 90-minute signature Himalayan hot stone massage and aromatherapy treatment at the resort spa. Celebrate the Poon Hill achievement with a private champagne toast on your suite's terrace overlooking the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike: Hot tea and energy bars at 04:15. Post-hike full breakfast at Ghorepani lodge: Eggs benedict, hash browns, fresh fruit, and unlimited coffee
meals.lunch: En route to Pokhara: Roadside authentic dal bhat at a local Newari restaurant — a genuine local culinary experience
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at resort's fine dining restaurant: Lobster bisque, pan-seared duck breast with Himalayan spice reduction, truffle risotto, and chocolate fondant with vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill sunrise is the highlight of the entire 14-day itinerary. October skies are typically crystal clear — ideal conditions. Dress in multiple warm layers as summit temperatures at dawn can reach -5°C to 2°C. The experience is absolutely worth the early wake-up.

day_by_day.morning: Rest & Recovery Morning — After the demanding Poon Hill section, Day 8 is intentionally lighter. Sleep in until 08:00. Enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast followed by a gentle 45-minute guided nature walk through the resort's garden, identifying medicinal Himalayan herbs with the resort's resident naturalist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Phewa Lake Kayaking & Fishing — Private guided kayaking experience on Phewa Lake with premium equipment provided. Explore quiet coves and forested shorelines. Optional catch-and-release fly fishing with a professional fishing guide on the lake's pristine waters.
day_by_day.evening: Pokhara Old Bazaar & Night Market — Explore Pokhara's historic Bagar area and evening market with a private cultural guide. Visit local artisan workshops producing traditional Thangka paintings, hand-knotted carpets, and bronze Buddhist statues. Enjoy curated souvenir shopping at premium artisan galleries.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast: French toast with berry compote, smoked salmon bagel, freshly squeezed juices, and a Himalayan herbal wellness shot
meals.lunch: Lakeside dining at Pokhara's top restaurant — grilled fish from Phewa Lake, garden salad, and chilled Nepali craft beer
meals.dinner: Rooftop dining at a premium Pokhara restaurant with panoramic mountain views — mixed grill platter, mezze board, and signature cocktails

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest and recovery day after the high-altitude trekking section. Listen to your body — if fatigue persists, the afternoon kayaking can be replaced with additional spa treatments at the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Annapurna Conservation Area Guided Nature Trek — Depart at 07:00 for a professionally guided half-day nature and wildlife trek within the Annapurna Conservation Area. Focus on birdwatching (over 478 species recorded in the region), identifying Himalayan griffon vultures, lammergeiers, and colorful sunbirds. Your guide is a certified naturalist with deep ecological knowledge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begnas Lake Exploration — Drive 15km east of Pokhara to the serene and less-visited Begnas Lake. Enjoy a private boat ride on this tranquil lake surrounded by forested hills and rice paddies. Visit the Rupa Lake wetland area, a designated Ramsar conservation site, for exceptional birdwatching.
day_by_day.evening: Private Cooking Class & Dinner — Return to resort for an exclusive private Nepali cooking class with the resort's head chef. Learn to prepare authentic dishes including dal bhat, momo dumplings, sel roti, and Nepali-style achar (pickle). Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Nutritious trekker's breakfast: Oatmeal with Himalayan berries, protein-rich eggs, whole grain toast, and green smoothie
meals.lunch: Lakeside picnic at Begnas Lake — resort-packed gourmet basket with artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class — dal bhat, steamed momos, and sel roti, served with premium Nepali wine from the Mustang region

day_by_day.notes: Bring binoculars for the birdwatching trek — October is excellent for migratory species. The cooking class begins at 17:00 and lasts approximately 2.5 hours. Request dietary preferences in advance so the chef can customize the menu.

day_by_day.morning: Annapurna Base Camp Helicopter Excursion — The most dramatic experience of the trip. Depart at 06:30 by private helicopter for an exclusive flight into the Annapurna Sanctuary, landing at Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) for approximately 20–30 minutes. Stand at the foot of Annapurna I, the world's 10th highest mountain, surrounded by a cathedral of 7,000–8,000m peaks in every direction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return & Luxury Recovery Afternoon — Return to resort by mid-morning. Spend the afternoon at leisure — choose from the resort's infinity pool, private spa treatments, or simply relax on your suite's terrace absorbing the mountain panorama. Optional: private journal writing session or photography editing workshop.
day_by_day.evening: Gala Dinner Under the Stars — Resort arranges a private open-air gala dinner on a specially prepared terrace or garden setting with candlelight, floral arrangements, and a live acoustic musician performing Nepali and classical pieces. A truly unforgettable evening.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast at 05:45: Croissants, protein bars, fruit, and strong coffee — light but energizing
meals.lunch: Post-helicopter late brunch at the resort: Eggs royale, smoked salmon platter, fresh fruit bowl, mimosas, and Himalayan herbal infusions
meals.dinner: 6-course private gala dinner: Amuse-bouche of yak cheese crostini, cream of asparagus soup, seared scallops, sorbet intermezzo, Wagyu beef tenderloin with truffle jus, and a decadent dark chocolate sphere dessert

day_by_day.notes: Annapurna Base Camp helicopter excursion is strictly weather-dependent. Resort will confirm by 20:00 the previous evening. At 4,130m, spend no more than 30 minutes at the landing site. Move slowly, breathe deeply, and stay hydrated. This is the crown jewel of the itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Sarangkot Paragliding Experience — For the adventurous, depart at 08:00 for a tandem paragliding flight from Sarangkot with a certified professional pilot. Soar above Pokhara Valley and Phewa Lake with the entire Annapurna Himalayan range as your backdrop. Flight duration approximately 20–30 minutes with optional extended flight packages.
day_by_day.afternoon: International Mountain Museum — Visit the world-class International Mountain Museum in Pokhara, the only museum in Asia dedicated to the mountains and mountain peoples of the Himalayas. Explore exhibits on Himalayan geology, mountaineering history, and the cultures of Nepal's highland communities. Private guided tour arranged.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Boat Cruise on Phewa Lake — Private luxury boat cruise on Phewa Lake during golden hour. Champagne, canapés, and a private musician aboard create an intimate and romantic atmosphere as the Annapurna range glows in alpenglow hues of orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Avocado toast, poached eggs, smoked trout, fresh juices, and specialty pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Museum café lunch or nearby Pokhara restaurant: Gourmet sandwiches, caesar salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Premium lakeside restaurant dinner: Tandoori mixed grill, garlic naan, saffron rice, and mango kulfi dessert

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding is weather and wind-dependent. Minimum age 16, maximum weight 100kg for tandem flights. The museum visit takes approximately 2 hours and is highly recommended for context on the Himalayan world you've been exploring. Book the sunset boat cruise through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Dhampus Village Trek — Depart at 07:30 for a guided half-day trek to Dhampus village (1,650m), one of the most accessible Gurung villages with superb close-up views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain). The trail passes through terraced farmland, oak forests, and traditional stone villages. Approximately 3 hours of comfortable trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Australian Camp & Kande Exploration — Continue the trek to Australian Camp (2,060m) for expansive panoramic views of the Annapurna range. Your guide explains the fascinating story behind the camp's unusual name. Descend to Kande for private vehicle pickup and return to resort.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Ayurvedic Spa Evening — Indulge in a comprehensive 2-hour Ayurvedic treatment package at the resort spa, including Shirodhara (warm oil head treatment), full-body Abhyanga massage, and herbal steam therapy. A deeply restorative experience for the body after 12 days of adventure.

meals.breakfast: Pre-trek energizing breakfast: Banana pancakes, granola parfait, boiled eggs, and ginger-turmeric wellness tea
meals.lunch: Gurung village home-cooked lunch in Dhampus — authentic local family hosts prepare dal bhat, vegetable curry, and homemade yogurt in a traditional setting
meals.dinner: In-room private dining: Personalized menu created by the chef based on your preferences — a relaxed and intimate conclusion to the day

day_by_day.notes: The Dhampus–Australian Camp trek is suitable for all fitness levels and is an excellent final trekking day. Bring a light daypack with water, snacks, and a camera. The Gurung village lunch is a genuine cultural exchange — tips for the hosting family are warmly appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure Morning & Final Mountain Meditation — Wake naturally and enjoy a final sunrise from your suite's terrace or the resort's mountain-view deck. Optional: one final private yoga session at 07:00 focusing on gratitude and reflection. Spend the morning at leisure — pool, spa, or simply absorbing the Himalayan panorama you've earned.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kathmandu Day Trip (Optional) or Pokhara Final Exploration — Option A: Private vehicle and flight to Kathmandu for a curated half-day tour of Pashupatinath Temple, Boudhanath Stupa, and Thamel's premium artisan galleries before returning to Pokhara.
